The '''2002–03 Bundesliga''' was the 40th season of the [[Bundesliga]]. It began on 9 August 2002 and concluded on 24 May 2003.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/competition/co12/se2747/all-matches/ |title=Bundesliga 2002/2003 » Schedule |website=WorldFootball.net |access-date=13 June 2020}}</ref> This was the first season where the defending champions kicked–off the opening match.<ref>{{cite news|title=FC Bayern eröffnet Saison gegen Wolfsburg|url=http://www.sueddeutsche.de/sport/bundesliga-fc-bayern-eroeffnet-saison-gegen-wolfsburg-1.2014038|access-date=18 July 2014|work=Süddeutsche Zeitung|date=24 June 2014|language=de}}</ref>

==Teams==
Eighteen teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top fifteen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2001–02 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]]. The promoted teams were [[Hannover 96]], [[Arminia Bielefeld]] and [[VfL Bochum]], returning to the top flight after an absence of thirteen, two and one years respectively. They replaced [[SC Freiburg]], [[1. FC Köln]] and [[FC St. Pauli]] after spending time in the top flight for four, two and one years respectively.
